relevance_note: Single-patient case report of an 11-year-old boy in whom 'a diagnosis of Alexander's disease (AD) was made' on clinical, imaging and biopsy grounds; no GFAP testing or variant is reported.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script in the scratch directory and spans checked verbatim by script. One in-scope person (the single unnamed patient, label 'patient'); scope is met by the diagnosis of Alexander disease, not by a variant. The paper reports no genetic testing and no GFAP variant for this patient (GFAP is mentioned only in the Discussion in general terms), so the variants table is empty and n_patients_reported (patients with a GFAP variant) is null. Age at diagnosis is not stated as such; the patient is 11 years old at presentation, recorded as age at last evaluation. Vital status is not stated explicitly. Hedged statements ('possible aspiration event', 'presumed pneumonia') were not recorded as features. The sepsis-workup sentence is split by the abstract in the converted text ('cerebrospi-' / 'nal fluid'), so it is quoted as two spans. Normal findings recorded as excluded abnormalities under D-27: 'metabolic studies ... within normal limits' and 'cytology and autoimmune studies ... negative' are recorded as the paper names them (no more specific abnormality excluded beyond the two named antibodies). Depressed mental status at intubation and a normal level of consciousness on arrival at the accepting hospital refer to different times, not a contradiction; both are recorded with timing in severity_or_detail. Checklist: internal/external capsule and dentate nucleus signal changes were not counted as basal ganglia/thalamic abnormality; periventricular white matter signal change was not counted as a periventricular rim. Contrast enhancement is taken from the Fig. 1 legend, which the text identifies as MRI images. No contradictions found in the paper.

study_type.span: This case highlights the importance of complete history-taking and examinations in pediatric patients.
